title: Give every component URN a valid layer value

facts.note: Task text mentions defining, reviewing or re-layering components.

values: any artifact declaring component URNs (plans, wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, component specs, docs)
facts.note: Any file containing component:… URNs; not limited to changed or plan-only files.
Diff-level observer extracting added/changed component:… URNs; one trigger, not the only one.

values: component URN with a layer value outside the allowed set
component assigned to more than one layer
facts.note: Needs a URN parser/validator against the allowed layer set plus a membership observer; the source declares implementation type none.

fires: Planner declares a new component URN in any planning artifact
Planner edits an existing component URN or its layer value
Any component URN (new or existing, changed or not) has no layer value or uses a non-allowed value such as "service"
A component is described as belonging to more than one layer
doesNotFire: Non-component URNs (e.g. wagon or acceptance URNs) that carry no layer by design
Work that neither declares, changes, nor inspects any component

given: A component exists or is being declared, identified by a component URN
when: The planner writes, edits or reviews that component URN
then: The component URN contains a valid layer value, exactly one of: presentation|application|domain|integration|assembly.
prefer: Put the layer in the URN's layer segment (in the source example it is the final segment), using one value spelled exactly as in the allowed set.
For reference, each layer has typical methods / consumes / produces listed in context.repo-topology.layers (e.g. domain: process, calculate, applyRules).
If a component spans layers, split it into one component per layer, each with its own URN carrying that single layer value.
avoid: Component URNs with no layer value.
Invented or synonym layer values (e.g. "service") outside the allowed set.
Assigning one component to more than one architectural layer (a component belongs to exactly one layer).
why: Pinning each component to exactly one layer keeps the layered architecture honest and lets the URN's layer segment be trusted as the single source of truth for where a component lives.
evidence: Each component is assigned to exactly one architectural layer.
Each component URN contains a valid layer value from {presentation, application, domain, integration, assembly}.
The chosen layer is consistent with that layer's typical methods / consumes / produces profile.
verifier_detail: Check: URN contains valid layer: presentation|application|domain|integration|assembly (exact allowed values; anything else, e.g. "service", is a violation; a URN with no layer is a violation).
Compliant source example: 'component:resolve-dilemmas:choose-option:OptionValidator:backend:domain' — one valid layer (domain), located in the final URN segment.
Counter-example: a component URN with no layer segment, or with an invalid layer like "service".

Layer patterns (from valid_layers term): presentation typical_methods [render, handleInput, updateDisplay], consumes [user interactions, display updates], produces [ui events, user actions]; application typical_methods [execute, coordinate, validate], consumes [commands, queries], produces [events, responses]; domain typical_methods [process, calculate, applyRules], consumes [domain events], produces [domain events, state changes]; integration typical_methods [fetch, save, publish], consumes [external events], produces [external calls, persistence operations]; assembly has no pattern listed in source.
Exactly-one-layer membership (term one_layer: 'Component belongs to exactly one layer') is a separate check: flag any component described or declared under more than one layer.

splitSuggestion.then: Each component belongs to exactly one architectural layer; a component spanning layers is split into one component per layer.

sharedNodes.text: Allowed architectural layers: presentation, application, domain, integration, assembly. Per-layer profile — presentation: typical methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: typical methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: typical methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: typical methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.

additions.text: The source statement holds two independently checkable obligations: (a) URN contains a valid layer value (kept in then) and (b) a component belongs to exactly one layer (kept as avoid[2]/evidence[0]/verifier_detail[5]); (b) should become its own convention planner.component.single-layer-membership.
additions.justification: One-obligation rule; auditor required separating membership cardinality from URN-value validity.
